## TL;DR

Settings now has a narrow-screen section chooser and a one-column, touch-friendly layout below the 720 CSS px boundary. The page continues to use its existing tabs, URL query state, configuration store, controls, validation, save flow, and error display. Desktop keeps its tab strip and existing composition. The branch also includes a defensive compatibility improvement to the shared responsive-layout composable for older MediaQueryList implementations and minimal test environments.

## Work and rationale

ADR 0011 calls for a single Vue SPA with distinct page compositions selected at 720 CSS px, using the same router, stores, and mutations. Settings already had a canonical seven-tab model and URL-backed active tab. The implementation therefore adds a mobile navigation view over that same model instead of creating mobile-only configuration panels or state. Each mobile button calls the existing tab setter, so selecting a section preserves route behavior and the desktop tab implementation remains available at wider sizes.

The responsive composable exposes `isNarrow` and is used to render the mobile chooser only when the viewport is narrow. The CSS breakpoint matches the ADR boundary. The chooser uses a compact two-column grid of clearly labeled buttons, with a minimum 44 px control height, visible focus treatment, and a selected state. It does not require hover. The desktop `.settings-tabs` strip is hidden in the narrow CSS composition, while remaining present and functional at desktop widths.

The narrow CSS changes arrange setting rows vertically and constrain their information and control columns to available width. Inputs and buttons gain comfortable minimum height, long text can wrap, section chips wrap rather than forcing a wide row, and activity animation controls reduce to one column. The page and child controls use `min-width: 0` and bounded widths to prevent common flex/grid overflow. Header actions and save/error text can wrap as well. These rules are scoped under the Settings page and the narrow breakpoint, preserving the existing desktop styling.

Coverage was added to the Settings save behavior test. It simulates a narrow media query, confirms the mobile chooser appears with all seven tabs, checks that section selection updates the route and active state, and drives the existing auto-save path into an error to verify the message remains visible. It also checks responsive listener cleanup. A separate desktop assertion checks that the mobile chooser is absent and the existing tab strip is present. Existing save-only-changed coverage remains in place.

The responsive composable needed a small compatibility adjustment because its listener setup previously assumed either modern MediaQueryList events or a usable legacy listener. It now tracks which cleanup is needed, uses legacy add/remove listener methods when available, and falls back to window resize events for minimal implementations. This keeps viewport state reactive across supported environments and avoids removing listeners that were never registered.

## Approaches tried

The implementation reuses the existing tab data and setter rather than duplicating the settings section list. It retains the established desktop tablist and conditionally adds only the mobile chooser. Styling is a narrow-only layer in the shared stylesheet, following the repository convention that shared page styles belong there. No configuration key, schema, store, save endpoint, or raw TOML control was introduced.

The review shot remains the declared desktop Settings route because it highlights preservation of the established desktop navigation. Automated coverage exercises the narrow chooser and interactions directly; the review record notes that a narrow viewport screenshot would offer additional visual evidence.

## Challenges and blockers

A previous handoff attempt failed its UI verification because the declared highlight `.settings-mobile-nav` did not match the page at the captured desktop viewport. The recorded task history says the shot configuration was subsequently corrected and UI verification passed; the current task specification declares `.settings-tabs` for the desktop shot. The earlier review was good to go and reported no bugs. It noted a possible one-frame state gap before the responsive composable mounts and that the hidden desktop tablist remains in the DOM on narrow viewports. Those are limited concerns: the CSS prevents desktop tabs from displaying at the narrow breakpoint, and the mobile navigation appears after mount. No review finding required code changes.

The latest handoff attempt was rejected before check execution because the engineering report draft was missing. This draft records the actual implementation and review history; the required changed-path check is being run for this handoff.

## Key learnings

A mobile composition can preserve complicated Settings behavior by sharing the existing section model and route setter, while changing navigation and layout at the viewport boundary. Keeping the change scoped to the page avoids perturbing shell navigation, which belongs to the dependent mobile-shell work. Responsive code should also handle older WebViews and incomplete test doubles deliberately, with cleanup paired to the listener actually registered.
